A maintenance release on top of v2.0.0: downloads now go to the right place, the UI language is
switchable (and English by default), and the Unraid template moved into a shared feed.

## Fixed

- **Downloads now land in the mapped `/downloads` share.** On a fresh install JDownloader wrote to
  its built-in `/config/JDownloader/downloads` (inside appdata) and ignored the mapped volume — no
  matter what host path the template used. Two causes: the default download folder was never set, and
  (the real one) a Docker-auto-created `/downloads` host path is owned `root:root`, which the
  container user can't write, so JD silently fell back to appdata. The container now **seeds
  `/downloads` as the default download folder** and **chowns `/downloads`** to PUID/PGID on start,
  with a clear log warning if it's still not writable.
- **The UI language now sticks.** It was re-applied on every container start, so a language picked in
  JDownloader's own menu was reset on the next restart. It is now seeded only on the first run, so
  your selection persists.

## Changed

- **Default UI language is now English** (was German). Change it any time in JDownloader's own
  language menu (Settings → the flag icon); your choice is saved and survives restarts.
- **Tighter template description** — a shorter Overview that leads with the dark mode and full
  two-way clipboard support.

## Packaging / docs

- The Unraid Community Applications template now lives in the shared
  [`unraid-docker-templates`](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/unraid-docker-templates) feed
  (one CA submission for all apps), and `<Support>` points at the Unraid forum support thread.
- Added app screenshots to the README and a versioned support-thread template (`.github/SUPPORT_THREAD.*`).

## Notes

- All settings, links and session state live in `/config` and survive the update — no reconfiguration.
- First start still installs JDownloader and the dark theme: wait for the `JDOWNLOADER IS READY`
  banner in the container log before opening the WebUI.
- If your `/downloads` host folder was created as `root:root`, this release fixes it automatically;
  you can also set it yourself once with `chown nobody:users /mnt/.../<your-download-share>`.
